target_audience: Advanced High School (AP Calculus) or First-year University Students

sections.title: The Mystery of the Tangled Equation
sections.content: Introduce the difference between 'Explicit' functions (y isolated) and 'Implicit' equations (x and y are mixed). Use a visual of a simple line versus a complex circle. Explain that while we can't always solve for y, we still need to find the slope (rate of change) at any point on the curve.
sections.example: Visualizing a 'Mathematical Rollercoaster' loop defined by x² + y² = 25. Note that isolating y creates two messy square-root functions, which we want to avoid.

sections.title: Prerequisite: The Chain Rule Secret
sections.content: Briefly review the Chain Rule, as it is the engine of implicit differentiation. Emphasize that when we see 'y', we must treat it as an 'invisible function of x' [y(x)]. Show the animation of d/dx acting on a function of y.
sections.example: If y is a 'mystery box' containing x, then d/dx [y³] isn't just 3y², it's 3y² · (dy/dx). Think of (dy/dx) as the 'inner derivative' footprint.

sections.title: Step 1: The 'Differentiate Both Sides' Blitz
sections.content: Demonstrate applying d/dx to every term on both sides of the equation simultaneously. Use color-coding: Blue for terms with only x, Red for terms with y (which require the Chain Rule).
sections.example: For x² + y² = 25: Applying d/dx gives [d/dx(x²)] + [d/dx(y²)] = [d/dx(25)]. This results in 2x + 2y(dy/dx) = 0.

sections.title: Step 2: Isolating the Target (dy/dx)
sections.content: Transition to algebraic manipulation. The goal is to get all terms containing (dy/dx) on one side and everything else on the other. Use an animation of terms 'jumping' across the equal sign and signs changing.
sections.example: From 2x + 2y(dy/dx) = 0, subtract 2x to get 2y(dy/dx) = -2x. Then divide by 2y to reveal the slope formula: dy/dx = -x/y.

sections.title: Visual Validation: The Radar Cat
sections.content: Apply the found derivative to a coordinate. Use a character 'Radar Cat' sitting at a specific point on the circle to calculate the local slope. Graphically show the tangent line appearing to prove the math matches the visual steepness.
sections.example: At point (3, 4) on our rollercoaster: dy/dx = -3/4. Radar Cat sees a downward slope. At point (0, 5), dy/dx = 0/5 = 0, showing a perfectly flat peak.

sections.title: Summary & Mastery Recap
sections.content: Summarize the 3-step workflow: 1. Differentiate everything (watch for y!), 2. Collect dy/dx terms, 3. Solve. Reinforce that implicit differentiation works even when the geometry is 'tangled'.
sections.example: A final graphic overlay showing a complex 'Lissajous curve' (a figure-8 shape) being solved using the same three steps.
